People's Majlis Committee Minutes

9th meeting of the Environment and Climate Change Committee

5 August 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis G (Committee Room 6)
Start time: 10:20

{Presiding: the Chair of the Committee; Member for South Maafannu constituency, Abdulla Rifau}

The Chair speaking:

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. I welcome everyone to the 9th meeting of the People's Majlis Environment and Climate Change [Committee]. The meeting is being held in Committee Room 6. Today's date is 5 August 2026. The time is 10:20. On our agenda today is consultation on how to proceed with the work on the Bill to amend Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). In that regard, deciding on a deadline for completing the review of the bill, deciding on advertising to seek public opinion on the bill, and deciding on sending letters to seek comments on the bill from the relevant offices. The second item is proceeding with the work on the Bill to amend Law No. 24/2020 (Waste Management Act). And if there is any other matter, consulting on those matters. So, Law No. 26/2020 is a task that was accepted on the floor of the Majlis this Monday and referred to our committee. So, we will have to set a deadline for this work and also set the ways in which opinions will be sought regarding the work, and send that deadline to the Speaker of the Majlis. Now, looking at the bill, it is not a very big amendment. It is an amendment brought to its board. Changes to the composition of the board, and the chair of the board, the CEO becoming a board member, and very small amendments of this kind. So, looking at that amendment, I do not see us having to do a great deal of work. I see it as something that can be completed by giving the relevant institutions some time to send their opinions. So, I leave it to your views. Since I could not announce the attendance when I started the committee, I will announce the attendance. I (Member for South Maafannu constituency, Abdulla Rifau), Member for Mulaku constituency Ibrahim Naufal, Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency Abdulla Shazeem, Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, Member for South Thinadhoo constituency Mohamed Alsan Ahmed, Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed, Member for Keyodhoo constituency Mohamed Niushad, Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig. So, at this point, the floor goes to the Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.
Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. Regarding this amendment submitted on the Utility Regulatory Authority, at this committee stage, what I propose is this. So, to seek the advice and views of the relevant parties on this matter, obtaining those views, their views and advice, by Monday, and, as a deadline for this bill, I propose that this work be completed so that the whole bill is finished and sent to the floor by 16 September.

The Chair speaking:
Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency, Abdulla Shazeem.

Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency Abdulla Shazeem speaking:
I second the proposal made by the Honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.

The Chair speaking:
Yes! A view has now been proposed on how to proceed with Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). And this proposal has also been seconded. Therefore, I will put it to a vote to determine the view on this proposal. (Voting) This proposal has been passed by the consensus of the members present at today's meeting. Therefore, what has now been decided for proceeding with this law is: 16 September as the deadline for the law. And until the 10th of this month to seek the views of the public and the relevant parties. So, I ask the administrative desk to proceed with that work. So, item 2 is Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act). Now, we will continue from where we left off the other day. Now, there is a comment on this law sent by MIRA. There will be a printout of this comment in the file in front of you. The Ministry had said that its comment would be received today. It has not been received yet. And along with that, the Economic Ministry has also said they would like some time, until this Thursday, to send comments

Yes! Thank you, Chair. Regarding this amendment submitted on the Utility Regulatory Authority, at this committee stage, what I propose is this. So, to seek the advice and views of the relevant parties on this matter, obtaining those views, their views and advice, by Monday, and, as a deadline for this bill, I propose that this work be completed so that the whole bill is finished and sent to the floor by 16 September.

The Chair speaking:
Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency, Abdulla Shazeem.

Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency Abdulla Shazeem speaking:
I second the proposal made by the Honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.

The Chair speaking:
Yes! A view has now been proposed on how to proceed with Law No. 26/2020 (Utility Regulatory Authority Act). And this proposal has also been seconded. Therefore, I will put it to a vote to determine the view on this proposal. (Voting) This proposal has been passed by the consensus of the members present at today's meeting. Therefore, what has now been decided for proceeding with this law is: 16 September as the deadline for the law. And until the 10th of this month to seek the views of the public and the relevant parties. So, I ask the administrative desk to proceed with that work. So, item 2 is Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act). Now, we will continue from where we left off the other day. Now, there is a comment on this law sent by MIRA. There will be a printout of this comment in the file in front of you. The Ministry had said that its comment would be received today. It has not been received yet. And along with that, the Economic Ministry has also said they would like some time, until this Thursday, to send comments

. So, we will continue from where we finished the other day. Amendment 13, right? The other day we finished at amendment 13. So, we will start today's work from amendment 13. 13- Adding a section after section 24 of the said law, as follows. Industrial waste management plan. 24-1 (a)- An operational plan describing how the management of waste generated at places where industrial work is carried out will be conducted shall be prepared by the owner of that place or the party managing that place, in accordance with the regulation made under this law. (b)- Implementing the operational plan described in subsection (a) of this section is the responsibility of the owner of that place or the party managing that place. (c)- The industrial waste management operation plan prepared under subsection (a) of this section shall be a plan prepared in a manner consistent with the National Waste Management Master Plan and with the waste management operation plans at island and city level or at regional level. 14- Adding a subsection after subsection (b) of section 25 of the said law, as follows. 25 (c)- In the regulation made under subsection (b) of this section, having regard to the types of waste specified under this law, setting the license categories, and specifying the principles and procedures for issuing a license of each category and the principles for setting additional conditions in licenses so issued. 15- Adding a number after number 3 of subsection (b) of section 32 of the said law, as follows. 32 (b) 4- Bundles of bags containing more than 50 plastic bags. Adding a section after section 35 of the said law, as follows. Parties not registered with MIRA. 35-1. 16- Adding a section after section 35 of the said law, as follows. Parties not registered with MIRA. 35-1 (a)- A regulation specifying the principles on how parties other than those registered for GST with MIRA shall spend the fee collected in accordance with this law shall be prepared by the Ministry within one year of this law coming into force, published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives and made public on the Ministry's website. (b)- In accordance with this law and the regulation made under this law, that parties other than those registered for GST with MIRA are collecting the fee on plastic bags in the course of business activities carried out in the Maldives

shall be ensured by the Ministry. 17- Amending section 41 of the said law as follows. Establishing waste management centres, 41 (a)- Any party shall establish a waste management centre only in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry. (b)- A site for landfilling as a means of waste management shall be established only in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry. 18- Amending subsection (c) of section 43 of the said law as follows. 43 (c)- Waste generated and produced on islands and in areas where economic and/or industrial work is carried out that are not within the jurisdiction of an inhabited island of the Maldives shall be taken to the waste management centre of an inhabited island of the Maldives only in the manner set out in the regulation made under this law. Removing subsection (d) of section 43 of the said law. Amending section 43 of the said law as follows. Importing waste into the Maldives. Section 44. What is being removed from section 43? Before the section being removed from section 43 is subsection (d) of section 43. The regulation on the manner to be followed in transporting waste from one place to another shall be prepared by the Ministry within 6 months of this law coming into force and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives. Yes, when (c) comes, (d) is removed. 20- Amending section 44 of the said law as follows. Importing waste into the Maldives. 44- It is an offence for any party to import waste of any type into the Maldives. 21- Amending subsection (c) of section 47 of the said law as follows. Subsection (c) of section 47- It is an offence for any party to sell, use or distribute in the Maldives hazardous waste or anything containing such waste, except in accordance with the regulations made by the Ministry under this law and with a permit issued by the Environment Regulatory Authority. Waste will have been defined. Amending subsection (e) of section 47 of the said law as follows. Subsection (h) of section 47- Except in accordance with the regulations made by the Ministry under this law and with a permit issued by the Environmental Regulatory Authority, hazardous waste shall not be recycled, have useful materials recovered from it, or be processed for any other purpose in the Maldives. Amending subsection (a) of section 63 of the said law as follows. Subsection (a) of 63- A party required to prepare a plan for managing waste generated from economic activities or an industrial waste management plan, such

a plan has not been prepared, fining that party an amount not exceeding fifty thousand rufiyaa by the Utility Regulatory Authority or by a party designated by the Utility Regulatory Authority. Amending subsection (b) of section 64 of the said law as follows. Subsection (b) of section 64- Notwithstanding what is stated otherwise in subsection (a) of this section, if the party being fined is an island or city council, or if an offence specified in this law has been committed in an area not within the jurisdiction of an island or city council, the money from the fine paid for such an offence shall be deposited into the Maldives Green Fund established under Law No. 3/2006 (Public Finance Act). Amending subsection (a) of section 76 of the said law as follows. Waste, (a) of 76- 'Waste' means anything that has ceased to be used and is thrown away... (After a short while) Amending subsection (v) of section 76 of the said law as follows. Of waste... 25- Amending subsection (a) of section 76 of the said law as follows. (a) of 76- "Waste" means anything that has ceased to be used and is thrown away or handed over to a particular party to be thrown away. This includes solid things, liquids and gases. 26- Amending subsection (v) of section 76 of the said law as follows. Subsection (v) of section 76- "Industrial waste" means waste produced or generated in the course of industrial work. 27- Amending subsection (ah) of section 76 of the said law as follows. 76 (ah)- "Environmental Regulatory Authority" means the Environmental Regulatory Authority operating under the government ministry entrusted with the responsibility of implementing policies on environmental protection. 28- Amending section 76 (an) of the said law as follows. Section 76 (an)- "Plastic bag" means a bag used for carrying goods, other than bags in which goods are packaged, made in a manner that includes oxo-degradable plastic and plastic made from synthetic polymers, as well as degradable plastic that decomposes on its own. MIRA has a comment on this section. From Maldives Inland Revenue, on (an) of section 76. In connection with the amendment proposed to ban plastic bags, it is considered that the law should clarify what packaging is. A bag in which goods are packaged is a plastic bag used by the party producing the goods to package those goods to the extent necessarily required for selling those goods. (After a short while) That

in the ordinary meaning of the word, tying a knot after putting goods into a bag may also be considered packaging. Clarify what a bag in which goods are packaged is. (After a short while) Yes! When it was time to vote, we paused, on the basis that after taking a break for the vote we would continue to finish the remaining sections. (After a recess) Thank you. After pausing for the vote, the committee has now started again. The Honourable Member for Gemanafushi constituency, Asadhulla Shihab, has also joined our committee. Thank you. We have now debated for a sufficiently long time on the amendment that came to section 28, on bringing changes to this definition or amending it. So, I will now read out how that amendment stands now, together with the debates we have had. Section 28, 76 of the law, amending subsection (an) of section 76 of the said law as follows. 76 (an)- "Plastic bag" means a bag used for carrying goods, other than a bag in which goods are packaged to the extent necessarily required for selling those goods, made in a manner that includes oxo-degradable plastic and plastic made from synthetic polymers, as well as degradable plastic that decomposes on its own. So, I will put to a vote those who support this change. Yes! Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa speaking:
Thank you, Chair. 76 (an)- "Plastic bag" means a bag used for carrying goods, other than a bag in which goods are packaged, also made of oxo-degradable plastic and plastic made from synthetic polymers, as well as degradable plastic that decomposes on its own. Here, since saying a bag in which goods are packaged makes the meaning somewhat broader, we are proposing that amendment in the way the committee discussed. :"Plastic bag" means a bag used for carrying goods, other than a bag in which goods are packaged to the extent necessarily required for selling those goods, made in a manner that includes oxo-degradable plastic and plastic made from synthetic polymers, as well as degradable plastic that decomposes on its own. So, I propose this proposal in that way.

The Chair speaking:
Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed.

Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed speaking:
Yes! I second the proposal of the Honourable Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa.

The Chair speaking:
Thank you. An amendment has now been proposed to subsection (an) of section 76. This amendment was proposed by the Member for West Maafannu constituency, Musthafa, and seconded by the Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed. So, I put this amendment to a vote. (After a short while) So, this vote will be put again only after also looking at the other sections. That is because the Environment Ministry has also said that it will send its comments on the amendment to us by 12 o'clock. So, we will look for a while longer before putting this amendment to a vote. So, now 27. What remains now are definitions, right? It can be done very fast. We will finish them all together and then, with the amendments, come back after a break and finish. So, now only a very small bit remains. 29- Adding the following subsections after subsection (at) of section 76 of the said law. 76 (au)- "Repairing" means bringing changes to the physical characteristics of things that constitute waste for the purpose of reusing those things. (av)- "Explosives" means poisons, poisonous gases, biological or chemical substances harmful to life at a certain temperature or pressure, and things or substances that explode on their own. (aw)- "Flammable liquids" means substances that catch fire at the normal temperature of that environment through things used to light a fire or things that burn, or that easily catch fire on their own at a certain temperature. (ax)- "Readily combustible solids" means things not included as explosives, which, without mixing with any chemical or mineral, or from the surrounding environment

, without bringing a change to that thing's weight, volume or pressure, readily catch fire through things used to light a fire or things that burn. (ba)- "Substances liable to spontaneous combustion" means things or substances that readily catch fire, during their transport, at normal temperature or pressure, when their temperature rises on its own or when the temperature rises in the air. (bb)- "Substances which, in contact with water, catch fire or emit flammable gases" means substances that, when those things or substances come into contact with water, catch fire on their own or produce a gas that catches fire. (bc)- "Things or substances that, by producing oxygen, contribute to the combustion of another thing or substance" means things or substances that, even if they do not catch fire on their own, contribute to the combustion of another thing or substance by producing oxygen. (bd)- "Organic peroxides" means liquids or solids that contain bivalent oxygen (-0-0-) in their chemical structure. (be)- "Toxic substance" means a substance that, by entering the human body or by contact with the body, may cause loss of life, or cause temporary disability or permanent harm to humans or living organisms. (bf)- "Infectious substance" means a substance containing, or that has the capacity to transmit, germs of infectious diseases to humans or living organisms, or a substance containing such a dangerous thing. (bg)- "Corrosives" means a substance that, on contact with a part of the body or with anything, causes serious damage to the part of the body it touched or to the thing it touched because of the chemical reaction that occurs. (bh)- "Ecotoxic substance" means a substance or things that, due to that substance being released into the environment and being absorbed and accumulating in the bodies of the organisms living there, cause harm to those organisms in the short term or long term. (bi)- "Economic activities" means work carried out in tourism, agriculture, fisheries and other economic sectors. Changing the places in the said law described as "Agency" to "Environment Regulatory Authority", and changing the places referred to as "Authority" to "Utility Regulatory Authority". 31-

In connection with the amendments brought to the said law by this law, the amendments that need to be brought to the regulations made under the new law, and the regulations that need to be newly made under the new law, shall be prepared within 30 days from the date this law comes into force and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives. 32- This law shall come into force from the day this law is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette of the Maldives. So, we have now looked in this committee at all the amendments proposed to be brought to this law. Now, the main concerns we too have here relate to the definition of "plastic bag" in subsection (an) of section 76, on which MIRA has also commented. And the wording defining "plastic bag fee" in subsection (am) of section 76. That is, the way it is described as a price. MIRA has also expressed concern about that. So, we have not yet received the comments of the Economic Ministry and the Environment Ministry. Yes! [They say] there are no comments at all from the Economic Ministry. And the Environment Ministry has told me that the comment will be received by 12 o'clock today. So, at this point we will, so, we will also take to a vote the proposal that was proposed just now and then pause. After pausing, we will then come back again; so, we will now put it to a vote. Amendment 28 proposed to subsection (an) of section 76, the amendment proposed by the Member for West Maafannu constituency, Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, to the amendment proposed to subsection (an) of section 76 of the said law, and this proposed change has been seconded by the Member for Vilifushi constituency, Hassan Waheed. So, I will put to a vote changing it in that way, changing it as now proposed. (Voting) Yes, thank you. It is [passed] by the consensus of the members present at this time. At this point, we will conclude this committee. And I also announce that a meeting of this committee will be held in this room at 1 o'clock today. Thank you very much.
